subject: Emotions
title: Shame and the Nervous System
description: A short lesson to help you apply Shame and the Nervous System.

hook.text: In intense shame, some people dissociate: they go numb, feel unreal, or can't think clearly. Shame shuts down.

buildup.text: Stephen Porges' polyvagal theory explains this: extreme shame activates the dorsal vagal 'freeze' response.

discovery.text: The freeze response is the oldest survival mechanism—playing dead. Shame triggers it to escape social 'death.'

twist.text: This is why shamed people go silent in arguments. They're not ignoring you—their nervous system shut them down.

climax.text: Healing shame requires re-engaging the ventral vagal system: safety cues, warm voice tone, and patient presence.

punchline.text: Shame isn't an attitude. It's a nervous system state.

quiz.question: What response does extreme shame activate?
